notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Resident 1 is painting a watercolor harbor at dusk on 300 gsm cold-pressed cotton. Preserve the lighthouse halo and focal point, bright reflection corridor, airy water, broken pale shoreline, and muted foliage. Keep the boat secondary and soft-edged, with only a few crisp accents. Test on dry scraps; let washes dry before glazing or detailing, and avoid reworking set paint.

Framing and care: use acid-free, lignin-free cotton-rag mat/backing; reversible kozo-and-wheat-starch hinges; spacers; float mount for deckled edges. Consider low-reflection UV glazing or anti-static UV acrylic with a spacer. Acclimate flat 1–2 days; keep at 40–55% RH, 18–22°C, and low indirect light. Store flat in a rigid acid-free folder with loose tissue; handle clean, dry edges. Photograph evenly with a grey card/color target and compare every 6–12 months. Transport framed work upright and secured; acclimate after temperature changes. Pencil-label an acid-free tag. Inspect hinges at framing, every 1–2 years, and when opened. Use room-level humidity control, not loose silica gel in the frame. Inspect backing externally; use two-point hanging hardware and lower-corner bumpers. Clean glazing with a cloth, no cleaner.
